identity.title: ALMA Observations of the IRDC Clump G34.43+00.24 MM3: Complex Organic and Deuterated Molecules

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have observed complex organic molecules (COMs) and deuterated species toward a hot core/corino (HC) associated with the infrared dark cloud (IRDC) clump G34.43+00.24 MM3 with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

evidence.quote: The phase center was (R.A.(J2000), Dec.(J2000)) = (18$^{\rm h}$53$^{\rm m}$20.4$^{\rm s}$, 1$^{\circ}$28$^{\prime}$23.0$^{\prime\prime}$).
Kurayama et al. (2011) derived the distance to be 1.56 kpc from VLBI parallax observations.
In this paper, we consider both possibilities.

question.value: What is the chemical composition (COMs and deuterated molecules) of the hot core/corino in G34.43+00.24 MM3, and does it resemble high-mass hot cores or low-mass hot corinos?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we investigate the nature of the hot core/corino in G34.43+00.24 MM3 from its chemical composition.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00656.S.
We observed G34.43+00.24 MM3 with ALMA Band 6 and Band 7 in 2012.

analysis_steps.goal: Image cubes and integrated intensity maps

method.value: Average channels, integrate over ±5 km/s about 59.7 km/s (wider for blended lines)

evidence.quote: the velocity range for the integration is $\pm$5 km s$^{-1}$ centered at the LSR velocity of 59.7 km s$^{-1}$

key_parameters.value: Blended lines: -5 km/s of lowest to +5 km/s of highest velocity line

evidence.quote: the velocity range for the integration is set from -5 km s$^{-1}$ of the lowest velocity line to +5 km s$^{-1}$ of the highest velocity line.

method.value: 2D Gaussian fit to integrated intensity maps, with deconvolution

evidence.quote: We fit a 2D Gaussian to the integrated intensity maps of the COMs emission near G34.43 MM3 HC in Figure 1
using the Gaussian fitting task in $imview$ of the CASA software package

evidence.quote: Hence, we exclude those lines (black circles in Figure 5) for the temperature estimate using the rotation diagram method.

evidence.quote: We use this temperature for the derivation of the column density of all the observed molecules, including CH$_3$OH.

analysis_steps.goal: Compare abundances relative to CH3OH with other sources

method.value: Compare X(CH3OH) ratios with hot corinos and high-mass hot cores from literature

evidence.quote: we use the abundances relative to CH$_3$OH, because CH$_3$OH is thought to be the parent species
The data were reduced by the CASA software package.
We estimate the optical depth of each line by using the RADEX code (van der Tak et al. 2007).
the rotation temperature is derived to be 110$_{-20}^{+30}$ K
The D$_2$CO/CH$_3$OH ratio of G34.43 MM3 HC is evaluated to be 1.5$_{-1.0}^{+3.1}$$\times$10$^{-3}$

findings_qualitative.value: Only CH3OH detected toward shocked regions; COMs not shock-originated

evidence.quote: None of these lines, except for CH$_3$OH, are detected toward the shocked regions in our data, which suggests that COMs do not originate in shocks.

findings_qualitative.value: DNC emission is offset from the hot core, likely tracing the envelope

evidence.quote: the DNC emission is likely to trace the envelope.

claims.hypothesis: Is the COM chemistry of G34.43 MM3 HC like high-mass hot cores or low-mass hot corinos?
claims.experiment: Derive COM column densities relative to CH3OH and compare with Taquet et al. (2015) averages
claims.result: CH3CH2CN, HCOOCH3, CH3OCH3 relative to CH3OH similar to high-mass hot cores; CH3CH2CN/CH3OH ~10x higher than low-mass
claims.finding: Warm-up phase conditions similar to high-mass sources

evidence.quote: the abundances of all the three COMs relative to CH$_3$OH of G34.43 MM3 HC are similar to the average values of the high-mass hot cores.

claims.experiment: Compare D2CO/CH3OH with other hot cores and hot corinos
claims.result: 1.5e-3, higher than NGC7129 FIR 2 and comparable to hot corino IRAS 16293 B
claims.finding: Implies young core and possibly long cold starless phase

evidence.quote: the high abundance of D$_2$CO in G34.43 MM3 HC would suggest a longer timescale of the cold ($<$ 20 K) starless phase than that of other hot cores.

claims.experiment: Check COM line detections toward shocked outflow-interaction region
claims.result: No COM lines except CH3OH detected there
claims.finding: COMs do not originate in shocks

evidence.quote: None of these lines, except for CH$_3$OH, are detected toward the shocked regions in our data

why_this_method.value: Abundances relative to CH3OH used because CH3OH is the parent species of COMs

evidence.quote: we use the abundances relative to CH$_3$OH, because CH$_3$OH is thought to be the parent species in the synthesis of more complex organic molecules

limitations_admitted.value: Distance is uncertain; resolution too low to resolve internal structure or confirm rotation

evidence.quote: Thus, the distance to this object is not well defined.
In order to fully confirm the rotation motion, we need higher angular resolution observations.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-temperature LTE at 110 K applied to all molecules; large errors
Blended lines and unresolved source size (beam dilution) not corrected
Scatter in rotation diagram; distance ambiguity affects interpretations
D2CO/CH3OH comparisons mix single-dish and interferometric data at different resolutions

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00656.S.
